items.title: Remi Wolf – “Twiggy”
items.summary: It's been two years since avant-pop musician Remi Wolf released her sophomore album Soup. Even though we haven't heard any new music from Wolf since, we know she's been busy: She collaborated with Thundercat last fall on the track "Children Of The Baked Potato" and, more recently, reunited with pal Hayley Williams at Bonnaroo last month and then Newport Folk Festival last weekend.

items.title: Yo La Tengo Void Scalper Tickets For Hanukkah Shows, Launch New Lottery
items.summary: Yo La Tengo recently announced this year's run of their annual Hannukah shows, slated for Dec. 4 to 11 at NYC's Bowery Ballroom. The pre-sale went down last week, and it was ruined by — you guessed it — scalpers! The band has since announced that they're voiding those tickets and launching a new lottery. The post Yo La Tengo Void Scalper Tickets For Hanukkah Shows, Launch New Lottery appeared first on Stereogum.

items.title: The Drums & Mareux – “It Didn’t Matter”
items.summary: When the Drums first emerged, I mentally slotted Jonny Pierce's music alongside bands like Beach Fossils, Real Estate, Wavves, and Best Coast — a guitar-driven complement to the summery lo-fi synth sounds we were hearing from the emergent chillwave scene. But the project has evolved a lot over the years, and his new single shows he could have just as easily been a chillwaver himself.

items.title: Ed Askew Didn’t Want to Paint It Black
items.summary: Ed Askew’s first album, a 1968 self-titled release (later issued as Ask the Unicorn), on the ESP-Disk label, was almost his last. ESP-Disk’s catalog of now-legendary jazz and avant-garde artists couldn’t keep it in business, and Askew had no luck placing his follow-up, Little Eyes.
